cases.prompt: Mid-task, the agent just explained a genuinely new, non-obvious platform/toolchain behavior the user hadn't hit before, and it's likely to matter again later in this project.
required_behaviors: asks 1-2 short questions back that require recalling or applying the concept, not just recognizing it
states its own expected/recommended answer alongside each question
waits for the user's answer before moving on
forbidden_behaviors: just restates the explanation and asks 'does that make sense?'
runs a long multi-round interview instead of one short confirmation round
baseline_expected_failure: agent explains the concept once and moves straight on, with no check
cases.review_notes: Fluency strength (feels understood) vs. storage strength (actually retained) is the point -- passive explanation alone does not build the latter.

cases.prompt: The agent just explained something routine (ordinary syntax, or something the user clearly already knew) during a task.
required_behaviors: does not trigger a teaching-moment check
does not log anything to LEARNING_LOG.md
forbidden_behaviors: checks understanding after every explanation regardless of novelty
logs routine explanations as if they were durable knowledge
baseline_expected_failure: agent fires a comprehension check on trivial or already-known material, turning the workflow into constant quizzing
cases.review_notes: Self-judged triggering only pays off if it stays selective; over-triggering is the main failure mode to guard against.

cases.prompt: The user asks for a full multi-session course on an unrelated topic (e.g. a structured curriculum with lessons, reference materials, and a resource list), not learning-alongside-real-work.
required_behaviors: recognizes this is a heavier, different request than the lightweight in-task check this skill provides
does not attempt to build a curriculum, lesson sequence, or resource list under this skill
forbidden_behaviors: silently expands this skill's scope into a full teaching-workspace/course builder
baseline_expected_failure: agent tries to stretch the lightweight check-and-log mechanism into a full course structure
cases.review_notes: Keeps this skill's scope narrow and distinct from a full teaching-workspace pattern, which is a materially different, heavier request.

cases.prompt: During a real engineering task, the agent discovers a genuinely new root cause (e.g. a platform restriction that explains a bug), explains it, runs the short check, and the user's answer confirms real understanding.
required_behaviors: explains the concept concisely before checking it, not after
runs exactly one short round of 1-2 questions with its own stated expected answer
on confirmation, appends a short entry to the project's LEARNING_LOG.md in the user's own framing, not a copy of the explanation
continues the original task afterward without turning the moment into a detour
forbidden_behaviors: skipping the log even though the concept was confirmed durable and relevant
writing a long transcript-style entry instead of a short reference note
blocking further task progress on the logging step
baseline_expected_failure: agent explains the finding well but never checks or logs it, so nothing durable survives the session
cases.review_notes: This is the end-to-end positive path: discover, explain, check, log, continue -- the whole point of the skill in one realistic pass.

cases.prompt: The agent is working with a user it has no prior LEARNING_LOG.md history with, in a domain neither has established a skill-level signal for yet.
required_behaviors: defaults toward checking more rather than less in the absence of any calibration signal
does not assume expert-level familiarity just because the concept feels routine to the agent itself
forbidden_behaviors: applying the agent's own expert bar as the default for an unknown user
skipping checks on the assumption that most users are already experienced
baseline_expected_failure: agent calibrates 'non-obvious' against its own knowledge, silently excluding real gaps for a junior or unfamiliar user
cases.review_notes: Zone-of-proximal-development framing: without evidence, the safer default is generous, not expert-calibrated -- a fixed bar tuned to one experienced user does not generalize to a general audience.

cases.prompt: The user reacts with surprise ('wait, I didn't know that') to something the agent had just treated as routine and did not check.
required_behaviors: treats this as a live calibration miss, not a one-off aside
explains and checks it now, the same as any other flagged concept
lowers the effective bar for that domain going forward
forbidden_behaviors: brushing past the surprise and continuing the original task unchanged
treating the miss as isolated with no effect on future triggering in that domain
baseline_expected_failure: agent notices the user was surprised but doesn't adjust future calibration, so the same class of gap keeps getting missed
cases.review_notes: The live feedback loop is what keeps calibration honest over a session -- a static initial guess that never updates isn't real adaptation.
